checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does process_checked_system_transaction raise InvalidBlock when system_tx_output.error is not None?

reachability.notes: If an attacker can cause a system contract (WITHDRAWAL_REQUEST_ADDRESS or CONSOLIDATION_REQUEST_ADDRESS) to revert, the entire block becomes invalid. If the error check is missing or bypassed, invalid return data could be committed.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all code paths where process_checked_system_transaction is invoked. 2. Verify that the function checks system_tx_output.error after execution. 3. Confirm InvalidBlock is raised when error is not None. 4. Attempt to craft inputs that cause system contract reversion and verify the block is rejected. 5. Check for race conditions or edge cases where the error check might be bypassed.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0011, Trust Boundaries: tb-004, tb-011. Post-condition property covering SG-009.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is process_unchecked_system_transaction correctly limited to beacon roots and history storage contracts only?

reachability.notes: Unchecked system transactions for beacon roots and history storage are assumed safe because their failure only affects ring buffer data, not consensus validity. A compromised CL could inject incorrect beacon roots without detection.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all call sites of process_unchecked_system_transaction. 2. Verify it is only invoked for BEACON_ROOTS_ADDRESS and HISTORY_STORAGE_ADDRESS. 3. Check that no other system contracts use the unchecked path. 4. Verify that failure of these contracts does not affect block validity. 5. Assess impact of incorrect beacon root injection on dependent smart contracts.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0012, Trust Boundary: tb-004. Invariant property covering SG-010.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does calculate_base_fee_per_gas enforce minimum increase of 1 when gas_used exceeds target?

reachability.notes: A proposer controls gas usage within their block. If the minimum increase of 1 can be circumvented, the base fee could stagnate at 0, allowing free transactions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate calculate_base_fee_per_gas implementation. 2. Verify the formula: when parent_gas_used > parent_gas_target, base_fee_per_gas_delta >= 1. 3. Test edge cases where parent_base_fee_per_gas is very low. 4. Check for integer division truncation that could result in delta of 0. 5. Verify block validation rejects headers with incorrect base fee calculations.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0013, Trust Boundary: tb-012. Invariant property covering SG-004.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are transaction validation checks ordered from general to specific (type, fees, gas, blob, authorization)?

reachability.notes: An attacker submits transactions designed to maximize validation cost. If cheap general checks are moved after expensive specific checks, the attacker can waste validator CPU. However, this is a low-effort single-peer DoS which may be out-of-scope.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate transaction_validation_dispatch in exceptions.py (SG-004). 2. Verify check order: type -> fees -> gas limits -> blob-specific -> authorization. 3. Assess computational cost of each check. 4. Submit malformed transactions to measure validation time. 5. Verify early-exit on cheap checks prevents CPU exhaustion.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0014, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Invariant property covering SG-004. CONDITIONAL SCOPE: Requires further investigation - may be out-of-scope as single-peer DoS.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Do all blob versioned hashes have version prefix 0x01 (VERSIONED_HASH_VERSION_KZG)?

reachability.notes: An attacker submits a blob transaction with versioned hashes that have the correct 0x01 prefix but correspond to invalid KZG commitments. The EL only checks the version byte; full KZG proof verification is performed by the CL.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate blob transaction validation in SG-005. 2. Verify that tx.blob_versioned_hashes is iterated and each hash[0] == 0x01. 3. Submit blob transactions with versioned hashes having prefixes 0x00, 0x02, etc. 4. Verify these transactions are rejected at EL validation. 5. Check that the validation covers all blob transactions, not just a subset.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0015, Trust Boundary: tb-008. Invariant property covering SG-005.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gas refund correctly capped at gas_used // 5 (EIP-3529)?

reachability.notes: An attacker crafts a transaction with operations that generate large refund counters (e.g., SSTORE clearing). If the cap calculation is incorrect, excess refunds allow the attacker to receive more gas back than expected.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate process_transaction (SG-013) refund calculation. 2. Verify formula: tx_gas_refund = min(gas_used // 5, refund_counter). 3. Craft transactions with SSTORE operations that maximize refund_counter. 4. Verify refund never exceeds 20% of gas_used. 5. Check for integer overflow/underflow in the calculation. 6. Test edge cases with very large gas values.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0016, Trust Boundary: tb-006. Invariant property covering SG-013.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7623 calldata floor gas cost enforced after refund calculation?

reachability.notes: An attacker crafts a transaction with large calldata but operations that generate refunds to pay below the floor. The max() ensures the minimum charge is met regardless of refunds.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate process_transaction (SG-013) final gas calculation. 2. Verify formula: tx_gas_used = max(gas_used - refund, calldata_floor_gas_cost). 3. Craft transactions with large calldata and high refund-generating operations. 4. Verify final gas charged is at least calldata_floor_gas_cost. 5. Check order of operations: refund applied before floor check. 6. Test with various calldata sizes and refund amounts.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0017, Trust Boundary: tb-006. Invariant property covering SG-013.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are post-merge header fields (difficulty, nonce, ommers_hash) correctly enforced as zero/empty?

reachability.notes: A malicious proposer sets post-merge fields to non-zero values to trigger pre-merge code paths. Three separate invariants (INV-005, INV-006, INV-007) enforce these constraints.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate validate_header (SG-005). 2. Verify checks: difficulty == 0, nonce == 0x0000000000000000, ommers_hash == EMPTY_OMMER_HASH. 3. Submit blocks with non-zero difficulty and verify rejection. 4. Submit blocks with non-zero nonce and verify rejection. 5. Submit blocks with non-empty ommers_hash and verify rejection. 6. Check both validate_header and state_transition for defense-in-depth.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0018, Trust Boundary: tb-005. Invariant property covering SG-005.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are transactions from accounts with code rejected unless the code is a valid EIP-7702 delegation designation?

reachability.notes: An attacker exploits EIP-7702 authorization list validation to gain code execution authority over accounts they do not control. If the delegation check is bypassed, contracts could initiate unauthorized transactions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate check_transaction (SG-006) delegation validation. 2. Verify that accounts with code can only send transactions if code is valid delegation designation. 3. Identify the delegation designation format (EIP-7702 prefix). 4. Attempt to send transaction from account with non-delegation code. 5. Verify rejection occurs. 6. Craft malformed delegation designations and verify they are rejected. 7. Check authorization list validation for signature verification bypass.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0019, Trust Boundary: tb-009. Pre-condition property covering SG-006.
